title: CI: bake model artifacts, sign manifests, and TTL-based pinning for staged profile publication
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Goal:
Implement a CI-driven ‘bake -> sign -> pin’ flow that produces a signed artifact bundle and an expiring pin (TTL) for staged performance profile publication. This ticket covers the pipeline additions and the manifest heuristics to create temporary pins for canary/validation runs, automatic retraction on regression, and safe promotion to permanent pins when criteria are met.

Background / Motivation:
We currently rely on manual steps to pin model versions and to publish performance profiles. That slows onboarding and increases chances of human error during fast model iterations. We want a CI step that: (1) builds/repackages the model artifact (container/manifest bundle), (2) runs reproducible checks (sanity hash, weight fingerprint, small perf smoke on unit shards), (3) cryptographically signs a manifest bundle, (4) publishes a TTL-based pin for canary traffic (e.g., 48h), and (5) on passing validation automatically promotes to a durable pin and publishes the performance profile.

Scope / Non-Goals:
- This ticket does not change the model training workflow or model registry schema.
- Does not implement a fully fledged attestation ledger; will plug into existing attestation API (ENG-72400 - placeholder).

Acceptance criteria:
- New CI job (GitHub Actions: .github/workflows/model-bake-pin.yml) that runs on model PRs and tags and does: bake -> sanity checks -> sign -> publish-ttl-pin.
- Signed manifest bundle uploaded to s3://redwood-model-artifacts/attested/<model>-<sha>.tar.gz and a signed manifest JSON in the same folder.
- TTL pin entry created in the model registry: {"model": "<name>", "pin": "pin-<sha>", "expires_at": "<ISO>"}. (Registry API stub available in dev.)
- Canary traffic routing docs updated with steps to route small % of traffic to TTL pins in Console runbook.
- Automatic promotion job that watches validation metrics (avgtoken-latency, edge-case-f1) and promotes to permanent pin when thresholds pass for N consecutive runs. Promotion must create an immutable release record.
- Rollback mechanism: if validation fails, the TTL pin is flagged for immediate retraction and a notification is sent to #runtime-alerts and the owning engineer.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Bake step: GH Action uses existing buildpack to produce a deterministic bundle. Produce manifest containing weight hashes, architecture, quantization metadata, and expected perf profile id.
2) Sanity checks: run unit smoke (1 request on small prompt set), fingerprint check, and content-address verification. Fail fast on mismatches.
3) Sign step: call internal signing service (signing-service.example.com/sign) with artifact SHA. Persist signature in signed-manifest.json.
4) Publish-ttl-pin: call model-registry API endpoint /pins with TTL param. Use sane defaults (48h) and allow override via PR label pin-ttl:72h.
5) Canary validation: schedule short validation runs (see validation harness in tools/evals) for the TTL pin. Validation metrics are emitted to the onboarding dashboard.
6) Promotion job: automated job reads metrics, evaluates gating rules (thresholds in config/auto-promote.yaml) and promotes by creating permanent pin and publishing performance profile.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for manifest generation and TTL payload encoding.
- Integration test in staging that exercises bake -> sign -> publish (uses test signing key and staging S3).
- End-to-end smoke: create a test model PR and confirm a TTL pin exists and can be routed.
- Chaos case: simulate signed-manifest tampering and ensure registry rejects retraction/promotion.

Rollout plan:
- Deploy pipeline to staging and run 10 synthetic model PRs for two days.
- Gradually enable on alpha models with conservative TTL (24h) and canary % = 0.5%.
- After 2 weeks and stable metrics, enable on all non-prod models and increase canary to 5% for 48h.

Open questions / design trade-offs:
- TTL length heuristic: fixed 48h vs heuristic-based (longer for large models). Decided to start fixed, but implement override label in PR.
- Whether to store signed manifests in the registry vs S3. Chosen S3 for replication speed; registry will store pointer + signature summary.
- Use KMS-backed signing key (recommended) vs ephemeral test keys. Production must use KMS; CI uses test key with rotation notes.

Monitoring & metrics:
- Number of TTL pins created / promoted / retracted.
- Time-to-promotion metric.
- Failures by stage (bake, sign, publish).
- Alerts: failure rate > 5% over 1h trips page on-call.

Related artifacts / links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONB/TTL+Pinning+Design
- GH Actions draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboard/pull/178
- Staging bucket: s3://redwood-staging-models/2025/ttl-test/
- Validation dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Onboard/ttl-validation

Tasks (checklist):
- [x] Prototype manifest schema and example bundle (Aditi)
- [x] Create GH Action skeleton and local runner tests (Marco)
- [ ] Integrate signing-service call and KMS config (Marco)
- [ ] Implement TTL pin creation in registry client (Infra/Registry)

Potential blockers:
- KMS access gating for CI runners (security).
- Registry API contract finalization (waiting on ENG-72401).
